answer: Attention-Debt Identity Gate: each new agent identity must consume a fixed quota of scarce verified human-attention slots, releasing them only after sustained, non-repeating interactions scored by reviewers (like grain carried across a dune). Unlike one-off fees, this accrues debt over time: a gale of fake accounts exhausts slots fast, freezing registration. Attackers pay ongoing reviewer-hours and forfeit a timber-sized cache of accrued reputation per identity, making mass creation slower and costlier than honest use.
